readability.summary: Every new Rust module, the TypeScript modules, the build script and the end-to-end test open with their purpose, boundaries and sources; every public Rust item is documented, as the lints require; comments say why a rule exists and cite it; tests name the behaviour they prove. Review against the final code bounded every wait in the host and channel tests, so a broken rule fails its test instead of hanging the suite, and removed an unused helper and an unused development dependency. The recheck before the commit read the code again against the records that assign work to TASK-009 and against the running window. It removed the lifecycle states that nothing used and rewrote that module's account of the host's lifetime, corrected the reason the window gives when the host has no private channel folder, and made the end-to-end test count the host's status entry only where the user sees it (TASK-009_EVIDENCE.md sections 9 and 11).

cleanup.summary: TASK-009 created one temporary artifact inside the checkout, by mistake: at 16:34:39 a command that imported the check runner ran without -B, and Python wrote scripts/test/__pycache__/run_checks.cpython-314.pyc and its folder, both ignored by Git; the record of the IDE's activity found them. The scoped cleanup of the first close removed exactly those two (logs/cleanup_first_close.json). Everything else stayed outside the checkout: Cargo built into /mnt/F/Nexees-toolchains/target/; the Desktop window was built in its desktop/ folder there and installed for testing in desktop-install/ and, for the hardening trials, in desktop-trial/; the tests' stores and channels lived in the system temporary folder, each removed when its test ended; the end-to-end test's private profile was removed by the test; the negative-test copies, the lockfile generation and the evidence scripts used the session scratch folder. At the final close, scripts/test/task_cleanup.py ran on the checkout with the same TASK-009 manifest, first as a plan and then with --apply and its record: it found both artifacts gone, removed nothing, refused nothing, and left in place 36 untracked files, all TASK-009 deliverables and evidence, each with its hash. The ignored files are the owner's IDE output (rust-analyzer's target/ and the Java extension's .gradle/ beside TASK-003's prototype), which is not task-owned and was left exactly as it is, and one link, apps/desktop/node_modules, through which the owner's editor finds the window's packages in the Desktop build folder; it was made after the owner reported the editor's error, and it stays. The disposable installation, the session scratch folder and the scratch Cargo folder of the wire-format probe are removed once this receipt is committed and pushed; the trial installation was removed by the trials; the Desktop build folder stays beside the Cargo target folder as a build cache. No pre-existing or user-owned file was deleted, reset or stashed.
